**2026-08-26T15:39:21Z** — rotation onto 3952 after 56655 vanished mid-lease · *MEASURED*

**2026-08-26T14:41:40Z** — code durability: mirror unpushed commits through the paste transport · *MEASURED*

- config: `haul 09a31fa→d4215cb; render box offline since ~14:20Z 2026-08-26`
- produced: tmhaul code mirror/recover/status; bank auto-mirrors on push failure; verified end to end: a clone of GitHub (25cc3ff, no codemirror.rs) took paste P2476760718, advanced to d4215cb, and passed 163 tests
- why: state had three durability layers and code had one (GitHub). With the bridge down, a harness fix exists only on a box that rotation is designed to discard.

**2026-08-26T11:32:55Z** — the bundle check raced the branch, twice · *MEASURED*

- config: `the sha is resolved once, pinned into refs/tmhaul/send-<stamp>, and that ref is bundled and fetched; the ref is deleted straight after`
- produced: the failing bank went through on the next attempt; pushes since are clean
- why: I fixed this once by narrowing the window and it fired again within a day. Two reads of a moving target are a race at any distance; the sent side of a 'did what I sent arrive' check has to be PINNED. Worth recording because the failure mode is expensive in a different way from a missed alarm: a check that cries wolf on healthy operation sends someone hunting a transport bug that does not exist.
- control: the git log is the control and it is unambiguous: ccb64ee committed at 11:30:09 by the heartbeat, 07eaef7 at 11:30:17 by the supervisor, and the check compared one against the other. No transport was involved

**2026-08-26T05:49:36Z** — two defects in one /proc predicate, and a swallowed discovery failure · *MEASURED*

- config: `watch_pid_excluding(skip): the supervisor's alarm pass counts itself, the watch --detach guard does not; credential targets() reports a mirror-discovery failure instead of returning an empty list`
- produced: no false supervisor_died since the fix; watch --detach starts again; the credential server installed on 56655 on the next pass
- why: One function, two callers, opposite meanings of 'is a supervisor running here?'. Fixing it for one broke the other within twenty minutes, which is the useful part: when a predicate has two callers, check whether they mean the same thing by it. And the discovery path swallowed its own failure — .unwrap_or_default() is .ok()? wearing a different hat, and it made a broken server indistinguishable from an idle fleet.
- control: the false firing and the refused start were both observed live before the fix, on this box, minutes apart — the alarm fired at 05:36:49 with a healthy supervisor running, and the guard refused at 05:43 naming its own pid

**2026-08-26T04:02:44Z** — a budget can be a meter instead of a countdown · *MEASURED*

- config: `Policy gains has_switch (default yes); job.rec sets budget_has_switch = no for the sweep; beat, status and the CLI drop the percentage and the switch line for a budget that has none`
- produced: the sweep reports 18093 evals / 9h 50m productive with no threshold attached, instead of '98.3% of the switch threshold' and, within hours, a false 'the switch is due'
- why: Yesterday I split the budget KEY so the sweep stopped spending the search's allowance, and reported that as the fix. It was half of one: the sweep still measured itself against the search's number and was hours from announcing a decision nobody could act on. Scoping who spends a budget is not the same as scoping what the budget MEANS.
- control: a test drives a switchless budget far past BOTH arms (20 productive hours, 200M evals) and requires switch_reached to stay false, paired with one requiring the default policy to still trip at exactly 8M — turning the countdown off for one budget must not turn it off for the search it was agreed for

**2026-08-25T22:02:42Z** — the supervisor_died alarm · *MEASURED*

- config: `samples already carry their writing node; the view gains supervisor_here and this_node, filled by state::with_this_box, and the alarm fires only when the run is active AND this box wrote the last sample AND no supervisor process is alive here`
- produced: fired CRITICAL against the real dead supervisor on 119098 before I restarted it; 12 alarms now, selftest clean; 146 tests
- why: The harness already knew — beat prints NOT RUNNING — and the alarm surface did not. A check that exists but is not wired to what people read is not a check. Also learned: pgrep -f matches the shell command containing the pattern, so my ad-hoc liveness checks could answer yes with nothing running; the alarm's /proc parse was right where my shell was wrong.
- control: four silence tests: a live supervisor, a box that does not own the run, an unchecked box (None must not read as 'no'), and an idle project. Without the ownership one this alarm would scream on the devserver and on every heartbeat box that merely reads the repo

**2026-08-25T20:50:07Z** — the supervisor reloads job.rec every pass · *MEASURED*

- config: `each pass re-reads the spec; a bad spec keeps the running config; a changed worker_cmd is refused as needing a stand-down`
- produced: two reloads observed live under a running supervisor: bank_s 600->660 at 20:48:05 and 660->600 at 20:49:06, both journalled; a deliberately broken spec left the supervisor alive and sampling
- why: I tightened bank_s, banked it, and reported it done while the running supervisor kept the old value: it had snapshotted the config at startup. Third instance in two days of 'the thing running is not the thing you edited' — stale binary, stale config, and a grep that lied about a binary. On this project the thing editing job.rec is a woken heartbeat agent with no reason to suspect any of that.
- control: the broken-spec arm is the control that matters — without it, 'reloads the config' is indistinguishable from 'crashes on any edit', and the reload would be worse than the snapshot it replaced

**2026-08-25T20:03:05Z** — two boxes lost mid-lease in ninety minutes · *MEASURED*

- config: `bank_s tightened from 1800 to 600; 36944 retired, 119098 provisioned and recovered`
- produced: no work lost either time — both last mirrors (dd110440a234, b6a77584fc01) were already on origin/main and recover found 123 files identical across the GitHub clone and the paste mirror. 24576 lived 7h24m of a 12h lease, 36944 lived 4h10m
- why: The failure rate changes the planning horizon. The harness was built around the 18-hour lease cap as the thing that ends a box; in practice these boxes died at 4 and 7 hours with no warning, so the LEASE is not the bound that matters — the BANK CADENCE is, because that is what is at risk when a box goes without standing down. Ten minutes costs about 10% of a cycle in banking overhead, which is worth paying while the rate is this high and should be relaxed if it settles.
- control: the 'nothing was lost' claim is checked rather than assumed: each vanished box's final mirror sha was tested for ancestry in origin/main, which is a different artifact reached by a different credential

**2026-08-25T15:34:31Z** — 24576 vanished mid-lease; rotated to 36944 · *MEASURED*

- config: `box unreachable from the orchestrator AND by ssh from devvm at 15:30Z with 4h of lease remaining; provisioned 36944, recovered, retired 24576`
- produced: recover found 111 files identical between the GitHub clone and the paste mirror; the worker resumed and the run continued; the credential server discovered and served 36944 by itself within its cycle, with no human step
- why: Second unplanned rotation, and the first one where the credential bootstrap ran end to end with nobody in the loop — yesterday's fix (discover boxes by mirror paste, not only by the repo) is what made that possible, since a fresh box still cannot push its own registration. Also worth noting what a vanished box looks like: ssh refused with 'Permission denied (publickey)' rather than a timeout, so unreachability does not always present as a hang.
- control: the loss window is bounded by the mirror timestamps, not by a guess: the last mirror was 15:00:10Z sha=7fd5d5fe5575, which is also on origin/main, so at most one banking window of RECORD was at risk and none of it was

**2026-08-25T07:41:20Z** — the credential bootstrap could not reach a box that had never pushed · *MEASURED*

- config: `credential serve now unions the repo's box registry with node names parsed out of recent TMHAUL-STATE mirror paste titles; the launcher's lock is PID-aware`
- produced: 24576 was discovered and served within one --once pass; before the change it sat DEGRADED with the server running and finding nothing
- why: A bootstrap must not depend on the capability it is bootstrapping. A fresh box writes its registration into the repo and cannot push it — pushing is what it needs the credential FOR — so the registry the server reads never learned it existed. The mirror paste needs only an x509 cert, which every box has from its first minute, so that is the announcement channel that still works when the one being bootstrapped does not.
- control: five parse tests including a stale announcement, a duplicate, the server's own name, and a title of the right prefix but the wrong shape — that last one matters because the parsed token becomes an ssh hostname. And the lock fix was proved from the failure: kill -9, confirm the lock survived, watch the launcher reclaim it

- config: `budget intervals now carry a budget_key from the job; totals are per budget; legacy rows read as 'unattributed' rather than being absorbed; job.rec sets budget_key = resim-sweep`
- produced: the archive search's budget reads 0 evals / 0s, which is true — it has never run under this harness. The 9705 evals and 5h 5m of productive time are the sweep's, and tmhaul budget now says so on a separate line
- why: The harness was built so a stall could not spend this budget, and then it spent five hours of it on the wrong workload — I caught it at 50.8%, about five hours before it would have announced 'the switch is due' for a job the condition was never about. 'Counts work, not time' is not enough; it has to count THE work the threshold was agreed about. The same sentence I wrote about stalls applies one level up, and I did not see it until the number was half spent.
- control: three tests: two budgets in one directory do not contaminate each other while the cross-budget total still sums both; a keyless legacy interval lands in 'unattributed' and NOT in the search's; and ten productive hours of the wrong workload does not trip the switch for the right one

- produced: cargo build -p haul -p resim works again on a clean clone; 131 + 21 + 7 tests pass

**2026-08-24T23:38:12Z** — banking the validator-car resolver bundle · *MEASURED*

- config: `sha256-verified bundle, fetched to refs/remotes/incoming/validator-car, merge attempted in a scratch worktree, then pushed to origin as its OWN branch rather than merged into main`
- produced: origin/validator-car = 4fb42ad6b228b814679f5718d29d34eb9ab3407e, byte-identical to the sha the lead named. A merge into main conflicts in 119 hunks across 17 files, all under tools/, none under autopilot/
- why: Two independent lineages: main carries agent C2's and vjeux's tools/tmauto and tools/ghost work, the bundle carries agent C's original lineage plus the validator-car commits, and no cherry-pick equivalence between them. Resolving 119 hunks of somebody else's engine source by picking a side would silently drop landed work — and in this project a wrong resolution produces plausible wrong numbers rather than an error. Banking it as a branch loses nothing, invents nothing, and leaves the adjudication to whoever owns tmauto.
- control: sha256 of the bundle computed here matches the one supplied; git bundle verify reports a complete history; and the push driver refuses to report success unless the sha the render box pushed equals the local ref's

**2026-08-24T20:57:11Z** — the bridge credential bootstraps itself · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmhaul credential check|serve|selftest; serve runs on the devserver under cron (@reboot plus every 15 minutes, one instance by lock dir), reads the box registry from the repo, and pushes to any live box that lacks the file`
- produced: deleted the credential from the running box twice: the first time the devserver's --once pass installed it (mode 600, 160 bytes, owner vjeux); the second time nobody intervened at all and the 5-minute cycle healed it within one period. In between, the status page said DEGRADED and banking_degraded fired
- why: An otherwise autonomous rotation with one manual file copy is not autonomous, and the goal is months unattended. The interesting part is the direction: an OD cannot reach a devserver, so this could not be a pull by the box that needs the file — the machine that HAS the credential pushes it, aimed by a registry the repo already publishes. Hostnames are not secrets; the credential never touches the repo, a log, a paste or an error body.
- control: tmhaul credential selftest is the arm that matters: a delivery to an unreachable host must REFUSE, its reason must be a category rather than a transport body, and an absent file must read Absent rather than ok. Plus the positive control of this box's own working credential, so the three refusals are not passing vacuously on a box where everything fails
